review_notes: assets/products/tailfin/ holds 156 files but only 31 are distinct images. Three generic marketing shots (a bare Cannondale, an 'R&D Division' portrait collage, and a rider pointing at a road) are duplicated 26 times each as the -2/-3/-4 slots of most products, and most size variants of a line share a single -1 photo. Every image path listed in an `evidence` array was opened; duplicates are cited once against the line rather than repeated per size.

There is NO AeroPack in this catalogue. The 39 products contain the CargoPack System and the SpeedPack System, which are the same architecture the AeroPack established: a thru-axle-mounted rear rack with a seatpost top stay, carrying a bag that is clamped to the rack rather than strapped to the saddle. Everything the brief says about the AeroPack applies to those two records, and it is spelled out in their `mount` blocks.

Two non-spec keys are used deliberately: `mount.requires` (an explicit list of the hardware a product cannot mount without) and an extra `dia` key inside `dims_cm` on cylindrical products (preserving the catalogue's existing convention alongside the len/wid/hgt triple the spec asks for). Both are additive; the spec fields are all present and correct.

Tailfin publishes no linear dimensions at all for the Frame Bags, Fork Packs, Downtube Packs and Rear Top Tube Bags - those lines are sized by a printable A4/US-Letter template with no labelled numbers. Those records carry `verified: false` and leave dims_cm at the existing catalogue estimate rather than back-computing from volume.
`render` block added per the amended spec. 22 of 39 products carry one; the 17 that do not are the 9 frame bags and 8 top-tube bags, all of which are zipped, non-rolling and fixed in height.

SCHEMA EXTENSION NEEDING RATIFICATION: the spec's `render` block only offers `hgt_cm`, but on Tailfin's bar rolls and downtube packs the variable axis is LENGTH, not height - they roll at the ends or at the top of a pack lying along a tube. Drawing dims_cm.len for the MTB Large bar bag would put a 72cm bag on the bars, which is the same category of error the CargoPack's 42cm height was. Those 9 products therefore carry `render.len_cm` instead of `render.hgt_cm`, populated by the same rule (minimum of the published range where one exists). If the builder only reads `hgt_cm` these 9 will still render at their unfurled length - please confirm whether `len_cm` should be adopted spec-wide.

`proprietary_mount` added to all 39 products: a string naming the Tailfin-only hardware required, or `false` for genuinely universal products. 20 need Tailfin hardware, 19 do not. This is deliberately separate from `fits`, which stays reserved for the spec's four values and is set to `rack_only` only on the 6 products that actually need a rack. Fork Packs, Cage Packs and Bar Cage Bags use proprietary Tailfin mounts but are NOT rack-mounted and DO fit a 56cm drop-bar gravel bike that has the relevant bosses, so tagging them `rack_only` would be wrong.

Frame bags: Tailfin publish no per-size fit chart at all - they replaced it with a machine-learning sizing web app. The one linear figure that exists for the range is that the nine models suit bike sizes 47-61 cm; it is now in every frame bag's dims_note. The design notes also revealed an internal size-specific CARBON SPACE FRAME (two rods along the top edge and under the zip, user-removable), which is what the visible rib in the studio photos is - now in every frame bag's details.rigid_structure.

ROUND 1 (11 Aug, cross-brand gauntlet): the assertion in these notes that Tailfin publishes no linear dimensions for the frame bags, fork packs, cage packs, downtube packs and rear top tube bags is WRONG, and it was wrong because the evidence had never been fetched. assets/products/tailfin/ held 37 distinct images; tools/harvest-brand.mjs now holds 485 plus 22 rasterised sizing PDFs, and every one of the 16 product pages carries a labelled dimension drawing. Records corrected against those drawings this round: 2 downtube packs, 2 fork packs, 3 cage packs. VOCABULARY GAP recorded rather than fudged: the panniers and fork packs taper at different rates on their two section axes and geometry.taper carries one ratio, so the pair is in geometry.notes and the mean is in the field.

ROUND 1 layer-C list, for whoever ratifies vocabulary: (1) geometry.crossSection cannot say 'flat on the top and the front', which is the Bar Bag System's whole silhouette. (2) geometry.taper carries one ratio where the panniers and fork packs measurably taper at different rates on their two section axes. (3) There is no way to require a HANDLEBAR TYPE, so the two MTB Flat Bar SKUs and the 11L/15L Bar Cage Bags render on a drop bar the maker says they do not fit. (4) Rack-mounted SKUs have no per-brand rack asset, so Tailfin's thru-axle carbon arch is drawn as a generic wire pannier rack.

ROUND 1 SILHOUETTE FINDING, framebag_half, 9 products, layer B and the biggest single shape fault in the brand: Tailfin frame bags are NOT the Apidura kite. Tall blunt rear end face at the seat tube, lower edge falling gently forward at ~9 degrees, deepest point at ~0.82 of the length toward the head tube, then a steep ~40-degree climb to a shallow front face. Only the forward 15-20% of the lower edge touches the down tube. framehalf.js derives its belly position from the down tube angle assuming the whole lower-front edge rests on the tube, which is true for Apidura and false here. SCHEMA GAP: the belly fraction has no field - geometry.taper carries the two end faces only - so a per-product profile term is needed before this can be drawn correctly. Also unmodelled: the V-Mount pads (3-4 along the top edge at 134/261/329/345/366 MM from the FRONT end, plus 2 on the lower-front edge) with cargo straps threading through them around the TOP TUBE and the DOWN TUBE - nothing touches the seat tube or head tube - The critique also called the -7 mm top tube reading on all nine products a penetration fault. It is NOT one, and this correction is recorded rather than quietly dropped: bagshot prints it under 'mounts on', not 'CLASH', because a bag is supposed to touch the tube it hangs from (tools/bagshot.mjs CONTACT_OK). It reads exactly -7.0 mm on 101 of the 103 products this slot draws for 35 brands, unchanged by any geometry change tried against it - a constant, i.e. the attachment gate being satisfied, not a bevel or a placement error.

FIT, framebag_half: the 3.8/4.5/5.3/6.5L Half Frame Packs are longer than the rig frame's usable top tube (~48 cm) and are drawn clamped to it, 2-10 percent under their published length. Tailfin size this range for bikes from 47 to 61 cm; the rig is a 56, so this is the range working as intended rather than a fault. Recorded per product in fit_constraint. Same call as the 3L Downtube Pack.

ROUND 1, toptube+toptube_rear (the eighth and last slot critiqued): the two Rear Top Tube Bags are drawn BACK TO FRONT - tall at the stem end, tapering to the seat tube, where the real bag is a sail tallest against the seatpost tapering forward. toptube.js already has a `rear` flag and it is correctly true for these products, so the fault is downstream of that flag, not a missing one. NOT fixed this round: that builder draws 101 products and an unverified change to it is how this project loses a round. Also open in the slot: every toptube bag is ~20% over on the perpendicular axis, and the three Long Top Tube Bags carry a measured taper in geometry.taper that the render does not show at all (85->50, 105->65, 115->68 MM).

mount.notes: CRITICAL FOR THE BUILDER: this does not hang from the saddle. The rack takes the whole load through the rear thru-axle at the dropouts, arches over the wheel, and is triangulated forward by two top stays to a clamp on the seatpost. The bag sits ON the flat deck at the top of that arch, its long axis pointing rearward (-x), and clamps down to the deck rails; it may be run fixed-to-rack or as a quick-release removable bag. The bag's underside is dead flat and horizontal - it does not droop, and the tail does not sweep down toward the tyre. Deck height is roughly level with the saddle nose.

details.not_boltable: explicitly not designed to be bolted - rubber cargo straps only
details.strap_kit: 2 x 18.5cm cargo straps + 1 x 14.5cm strap; seatpost strap optional

mount.notes: Fully universal, strap-only. Sits on top of the top tube directly in front of the seatpost, tall end backward. The reduced height is specifically to let a dropper post travel past - relevant if the build has one.
